consequence.statement: After upgrading to 1.13.0 with default configuration, policy exceptions are disabled, so existing PolicyException resources stop being honoured and no longer exempt resources from policies until the operator follows the upgrade guidance to re-enable exceptions and configure the allowed namespace.
consequence.remediation: Follow the Kyverno 1.13 upgrade guidance linked from the release notes to re-enable policy exceptions and configure the namespace in which exceptions may be created (CVE-2024-48921).

assertion.statement: Removal of insecure configuration for exceptions: In prior versions, policy exceptions were allowed in all namespaces

evidence.locator: L551-L555 (Other Features and Enhancements › Security Hardening › Removal of insecure configuration for exceptions)
evidence.excerpt:
#### Removal of insecure configuration for exceptions

In prior versions, policy exceptions were allowed in all namespaces. This creates a potential security issue, as any user with permission to create a policy exception can bypass policies, even in other namespaces. See [CVE-2024-48921](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/security/advisories/GHSA-qjvc-p88j-j9rm) for more details.

This release changes the defaults to disable the policy exceptions and only allows exceptions to be created in a specified namespace. To maintain backward compatibility follow the [upgrade guidance](https://main.kyv…
